messages:
anna_partnerships: Heads up — CloudHub's marketplace PO is failing our vendor intake. Their AP system rejects the payee name. They sent PO -> 'Redwood Labs' but our contract and tax docs are 'Redwood Inference, Inc.' They say they can't change PO format on their side without a procurement ticket and it will delay listing.

natalie_procurement: Can you attach the PO PDF? need to check exact payee string and PO number.

anna_partnerships: Attached the PO in #ops but pasting relevant line: `Payee: Redwood Labs (doing business as Redwood Inference)` — CloudHub's AP parsing doesn't accept parentheses. PO#: CH-789012.

mike_finance: If it's a pure formatting/alias issue, finance can accept the invoice to match the PO if legal signs an acceptance memo. Need to know if 'Redwood Labs' is a registered DBA.

james_legal: Quick read: contract parties use 'Redwood Inference, Inc.' No DBA on file. We can do a one‑page amendment or a short acceptance letter acknowledging the PO and mapping payee -> legal entity. I'll draft a short template.

sarah_sales: CloudHub procurement already said they won't sign contract amendments right now — they only accept PO changes. They asked whether we can just accept invoices against that PO as-is.

natalie_procurement: That's risky without legal ack. We need traceability for audits. Is the acceptance letter sufficient for auditors?

james_legal: Yes, an acceptance memo that references PO# and states 'Redwood Labs = Redwood Inference, Inc. for purposes of this PO' and signed by our legal ops will work. I'll add a clause to flag tax/name consistency. Template below — please review:``` 
Acceptance of Purchase Order CH-789012
Redwood Inference, Inc. ("Seller") acknowledges that the Purchase Order issued by CloudHub ("Buyer") lists the payee as "Redwood Labs." For the purposes of Purchase Order CH-789012, "Redwood Labs" shall be understood to refer to Redwood Inference, Inc., a California corporation (EIN XX-XXXXXXX). This acceptance does not alter the underlying contract between the parties.
Signature: ___________________
Name: James (Legal)
Date: __________
``` 

anna_partnerships: That looks good. Can you make it 1) one‑page, 2) PDF-ready, 3) include a line for finance contact?

james_legal: Will do. Adding: "Finance contact: accounting@redwood.com" and small notarization block.

mike_finance: If legal signs and we attach the acceptance to the invoice/PO, finance will process payments against PO CH-789012. Requirements: PO number on invoice, invoice to contain buyer info, cc accounting@redwood.com, and include the signed acceptance letter.

sarah_sales: I'll ping CloudHub CSM and ask them to re-submit with the PO unchanged but attach our acceptance letter. Pinging @CloudHub-Procurement contact now. :phone: :eyes:

anna_partnerships: Quick ask — can we get the signed acceptance by EOD? CloudHub is targeting the marketplace publish for tomorrow morning.

james_legal: I can sign EOD. Natalie, can you prep the internal approval so legal can sign?

natalie_procurement: On it — routing to procurement head for approval now. ETA 3 hours.

dealbot: Escalation created: E-5423 — "CloudHub PO payee mismatch / acceptance memo required". Assigned: legal, finance, partnerships, procurement. SLA: 8h.

anna_partnerships: Thanks everyone. I'll coordinate with CloudHub and confirm once they attach our signed letter. :pray: 

mike_finance: FYI — once accepted, finance will tolerate the 'Redwood Labs' payee for this vendor-only PO, but please ensure future contracts use the legal name to avoid repeating this.

sarah_sales: Noted — updating partner onboarding checklist to validate payee naming in PO templates. :memo:

anna_partnerships: Closing loop later with final status. If anyone sees other blockers (tax form, W-9 mismatch), flag here.
